Triage first-touch grading (finding centralized round, 2026-08-20, triage seat session `session_016A4EBi3ky1mjTi6vD2kCvA`): **promote to `pm:queue`**, type Bug. Re-verified on `origin/main`: `ViewColumnInspector.tsx:157` still preserves whichever spelling the stored doc carries, so editing a legacy `accessorKey` column re-saves a spelling the strict `ListColumnSchema` refuses and post-#5068 ObjectGrid won't render — the editor keeps alive the dialect the renderer already gave up. Normalize-on-write is decidable *now* for grid view columns regardless of the #5120 data-table ruling (that contract is already settled: `field`/`label`), and fixing the editor shrinks the population #5349 must serve. One-file diff; sequence with/before #5349 as its card already requests.

**Why this card waited a round:** it was deferred from round 11 solely because #5596 was editing this directory's barrel. That PR is enqueued; the collision is cleared. Re-derive the file's state on the current tip — #5596 landed changes in `metadata-admin/`.

**Clause ②:** likely not tripped (a designer inspector, not a published declaration) — but **measure it rather than inherit my guess**. This seat has stated a reachability fact from memory and been wrong three times in two rounds. The test that decides it: does `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` re-export this module, and does the `exports` map reach it? `export *` propagates without naming, so a grep for the symbol in a barrel proves nothing.

**The judgement fork, stated up front.** The file preserves whichever spelling the stored document already used (`'field' in col || !('accessorKey' in col) ? 'field' : 'accessorKey'`). #5068 retired `ObjectGrid`'s undeclared `accessorKey`/`header` tolerance and migrated its one in-repo producer. If converging the writeback onto the canonical spelling would **change what a stored document becomes on next save**, that is a data-shape decision, not a refactor — **report it with the measurement rather than picking a side.**

**NEEDS DECISION — escalated to the maintainer** (`domain:ui` seat PM, reviewer of record). No PR, no code change, clean tree. The dispatch told the dev to report this fork rather than pick it, and it did — but the measurement changed what the fork *is*, so this is not the card as filed.

## The card's own severity note is wrong, and that is the finding

The issue says *"nothing is broken today by this alone"* and calls the two spellings a **round-trip**. Measured on the real component — mounted, one identity edit driven through the real controls, the actual `onPatch` payload captured and run through `ViewMetadataSchema` (the same gate `ResourceEditPage` uses, `clientValidation.ts:579`, mode `edit`):

| stored column | after one inspector edit | parses before | parses after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{accessorKey, header, width}` | `{accessorKey:'title', header, width}` | **false** | **false** |
| `{accessorKey, header, width}` (label edit) | `{accessorKey, header:'Title', width}` | **false** | **false** |
| `{accessorKey, label}` | `{accessorKey:'title', label}` | **false** | **false** |
| `{field, header}` | `{field, header:'Title'}` | **false** | **false** |
| **control** `{field, label, width}` | `{field:'title', label, width}` | true | true |
| **control** bare string `'name'` | `'title'` | true | true |

It is not a round-trip. It is a **closed loop**: the document is already refused before the edit and still refused after, because `patchIdentity` re-emits the spelling it found. **No sequence of inspector edits can turn such a column into a saveable document.** The two controls prove the instrument can produce `true`, and one of them caught a real bug in the harness on its first run.

## A fourth option the issue does not list, and it may be the whole fix

The file also carries the **READ** half of the same tolerance alias — `:64` `c.field ?? c.accessorKey`, `:68` `c.label ?? c.header`. That is literally the construct #5068 retired from `ObjectGrid`, still present one layer up, and it is *why the loop is invisible*: the inspector displays `'name'` as the column's field key for a document whose field key the spec says does not exist.

**Option D — retire the read tolerance too.** A legacy column then shows an empty field key and the author re-authors it: no silent rewrite of stored bytes, no cross-vocabulary fold. **It is the only branch consistent with both in-repo authorities at once**, which is why it belongs on the ballot.

## Why the write half is not this seat's to decide: two authorities point opposite ways

- `plugin-grid/columnSpellingDiagnostics.ts` + `ObjectGrid.tsx:1592-1625` (#5068 inheriting #3951) — **unify at the producer, no consumer-side tolerance.**
- `packages/core/src/utils/column-identity.ts:36-47` — `accessorKey` is deliberately **outside** the identity fold (*"the fold neither reads nor writes it"*); canonicalizing across that boundary *"would fossilize the merge"*. And `:160-172` records that for the analogous legacy retirement the repo chose **mirror-not-delete**, because columns entries cross into third-party renderers and *"dropping `name` from under them is a breaking change we have no inventory for."*

Option A (normalize on write) makes every legacy shape parse on the first identity edit and leaves canonical documents byte-identical — but it can only migrate `accessorKey`'s value by **reading it as identity**, which is exactly what `column-identity.ts` forbids. If A is chosen, that docblock must be amended in the same PR or the tree carries two contradicting rules.

## Two measured facts the maintainer should have before ruling

1. **In-repo population of `accessorKey`-shaped view columns is ZERO** on the current tip — re-confirmed with fixed-string search; every `accessorKey` hit belongs to the `table` / `data-table` component, which legitimately declares the key, and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx:90` actively teaches *"There is no `accessorKey`"* for `ListColumn`. So **option A's entire value rests on legacy tenant documents predating #4001** — the unmeasured population that made core choose mirror-not-delete.
2. **Save is not gated on this.** `ResourceEditPage`'s Save is disabled only by `inspectorBlocking`, fed exclusively by `onBlockingIssuesChange` — and `ViewColumnInspector` never sends it (it does not accept the prop). The Zod issues are banner/inline display only, so the refused document **is handed to the server**, and the server's verdict is authoritative. That last link lives in objectstack and is the one thing this seat could not measure.

## Reachability, measured rather than recalled — and the asymmetry matters

`grep -rn "^export \* " packages/app-shell/src` returns **zero**, so there is no export-star in this package and a name-based barrel check is sound here (that is the check I warned could be meaningless; it was verified applicable before being relied on). `ViewColumnInspector` appears **0** times in `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.js` — control symbol `registerMetadataInspector` appears 1 and 1. The `exports` map declares only `.` and `./styles.css`, and real `createRequire` resolution of every deep path fails `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`.

**But the behaviour is published.** `inspectors/index.ts` registers `ViewInspector` under `'view'` via `registerBuiltinInspectors()`, `getMetadataInspector` **is** a named export of the package root, and `ViewInspector` routes `selection.kind === 'column'` straight to this component. So no consumer can import or override it, yet every consumer of the package root gets its writeback behaviour in their designer. **Clause ② is not tripped** (no published declaration moves), but that asymmetry is what makes this a product decision rather than an internal refactor.

## The ruling needed

> **Is there a known population of pre-#4001 stored view documents carrying `accessorKey` columns?**

- **Yes** → **A + D**: normalize on write *and* drop the read alias, with `column-identity.ts:36-47`'s docblock amended in the same PR.
- **No** → **D alone**; the write half is moot, and A would be dead code.

The dev's recommendation is A+D conditional on that population existing, and it explicitly declined to take it. I agree with the analysis and am not overriding it: the deciding axis is a fact about stored tenant data that neither of us can see from this repo.

Option B (A plus a visible migration note) additionally needs user-facing copy in all ten `@object-ui/i18n` locale packs, which widens the file surface beyond this card.
